facts.statement: Stegopelta is a genus of nodosaurid dinosaur belonging to the struthiosaurin group.
facts.quote: Stegopelta (meaning "roofed shield") is a genus of struthiosaurin nodosaurid dinosaur

facts.statement: The genus is known from a partial skeleton found in the Frontier Formation of Fremont County, Wyoming, USA.
facts.quote: based on a partial skeleton from the Cretaceous (latest Albian-earliest Cenomanian) Belle Fourche Member of the Frontier Formation of Fremont County, Wyoming, USA.

facts.statement: Samuel Wendell Williston described the genus Stegopelta in 1905 based on the specimen FMNH UR88.
facts.quote: In 1905, Samuel Wendell Williston described FMNH UR88, a partial armored dinosaur skeleton

facts.statement: The original fossil specimen was in poor condition due to erosion and damage from cattle.
facts.quote: The specimen was in poor condition, as it had eroded from a slope and been walked on by cattle.

facts.statement: Williston compared the new genus to Stegosaurus and its armor to that of the mammal Glyptodon.
facts.quote: Williston compared his new genus to Stegosaurus, and the armor to that of Glyptodon.

facts.statement: Roy Lee Moodie redescribed the genus in 1910 and suggested it might be the same as Ankylosaurus.
facts.quote: Roy Lee Moodie redescribed it in 1910, and considered it to be close to, if not the same as, Ankylosaurus.

facts.statement: Walter Coombs synonymized Stegopelta with Nodosaurus in 1978.
facts.quote: Walter Coombs synonymized it with the more famous but equally poorly known Nodosaurus in his 1978 redescription of the Ankylosauria.

facts.statement: Ken Carpenter and James Kirkland reinstated Stegopelta as a valid genus in 1998 based on distinct vertebral and armor features.
facts.quote: It was reinstated as a valid genus by Ken Carpenter and James Kirkland (1998), who recognized it as having distinct vertebral and armor characteristics.

facts.statement: Tracy Ford assigned Stegopelta to the new subfamily Stegopeltinae in 2000, a classification not generally accepted.
facts.quote: Tracy Ford took this further in 2000, assigning it to a new subfamily in Ankylosauridae based on armor characteristics, which he called Stegopeltinae.

facts.statement: Stegopelta is classified within the family Nodosauridae.
Stegopelta lived during the middle Cretaceous, approximately 110 to 95 million years ago.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 110 y 95 millones de años, en el Albiense y Cenomaniense

facts.statement: Stegopelta was an armored dinosaur about 4.5 meters long, 1.6 meters high, and weighing 1000 kilograms.
facts.quote: Stegopelta fue un dinosaurio acorazado de alrededor de 4,5 metros de largo 1,6 de alto y un peso de 1000 kilogramos.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Stegopelta is related to the Shamosaurinae subfamily.
facts.quote: Por otro lado puede ser un anquilosáurido emparentado con Shamosaurinae.

facts.statement: The shape of the cervical vertebrae suggests a possible link with Texasetes.
facts.quote: La forma de los cervicales sugiere un lazo posible con Texasetes.

facts.statement: The fossil record for Stegopelta spans from 100.5 to 93.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Cenomanian (100.5 to 93.9 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Stegopelta was a slow quadrupedal herbivore that fed low to the ground and relied on its armor for defense.
rejected.quote: Since it is extremely unknown, at this point all there is to be said about the habits and life of Stegopelta is that it was a slow quadrupedal herbivore which fed low to the ground and relied on its armor for defense.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'fed low to the ground and relied on'

rejected.statement: The armor of Stegopelta included a fused region over the sacrum and shoulder spines that may have been split.
rejected.quote: Its armor included a fused region over the sacrum, and shoulder spines that may have been split, as seen in Edmontonia.
